headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared retrieval/content flow; no direct filesystem-write conflict, but MCP/API pathways raise cascading-error and compliance concerns.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Khoj ingests indexed documents and can use web search, while MemMachine exposes an MCP server and conversational context. That creates a plausible path where attacker-controlled content from Khoj’s notes/docs or retrieved sources is forwarded into MemMachine as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance filtering, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Khoj indexes attacker-controlled notes or web content that MemMachine later consumes as prompts, injection is possible.
IF MemMachine accepts MCP-fed text without provenance tagging, the bridge becomes instruction-like.
mitigations: Disable automatic forwarding of retrieved text between agents.
Add a provenance prefix to all cross-agent content.
Restrict Khoj to trusted collections only.
Require manual review before MemMachine acts on Khoj output.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents and has broad network egress; MemMachine handles long-term user facts and conversational context and can call APIs via MCP. If either agent forwards the other’s sensitive context to its backend or external services, leakage can occur in default workflows. The pairwise interaction is undocumented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Khoj sends indexed notes to external search or model services, those notes can leave the local boundary.
IF MemMachine forwards conversational context through MCP/API calls, user facts can be exposed to third parties.
mitigations: Limit both agents to local-only backends.
Exclude sensitive folders from Khoj indexing.
Turn off external search providers in Khoj.
Audit MemMachine MCP targets and allowlist only trusted endpoints.
requires-engineering: enforce per-field redaction before any API call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Khoj cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, so it cannot directly contend for mutable local resources. MemMachine’s profile only shows MCP/API access and no write-capable local storage. The overlap is therefore mostly read/context sharing, not a strong write-write conflict; low is the highest plausible severity.
conditions: IF MemMachine is configured with write-capable MCP tools to the same resources Khoj reads, contention could appear.
IF an external orchestrator grants both agents shared mutable scopes, conflicts increase.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible.
Separate their working directories.
Avoid shared git repositories for either agent.
Review MCP tool permissions before enabling writes.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj produces retrieved answers from notes/docs, and MemMachine is an agent that can act through REST, SDK, or MCP. If MemMachine treats Khoj output as authoritative, a retrieval error can cascade into downstream actions or recommendations. Because no verification layer is documented, medium is warranted rather than low.
conditions: IF MemMachine consumes Khoj summaries without independent verification, retrieval mistakes can propagate.
IF MemMachine uses those outputs to drive user-facing actions, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require source links in every Khoj-derived answer.
Add a verification step before MemMachine acts.
Use confidence thresholds for cross-agent handoffs.
Flag low-confidence retrieval results for manual review.
requires-engineering: implement structured citations and validation checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly handles personal notes and indexed documents, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. If the pair is used on regulated or retention-sensitive data, mismatched logging or retention policies can create compliance gaps. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so medium—not high—is the safest supported choice.
conditions: IF either agent retains user data longer than the other, deletion/export obligations can diverge.
IF regulated personal data is indexed in Khoj and mirrored into MemMachine context, policy scope widens.
mitigations: Publish retention settings for both agents.
Avoid storing regulated data in either agent.
Test delete/export flows on a sample record.
Align logging policies across both systems.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention.
